market_mood: Escalating Middle East conflict — Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, an Aramco HQ evacuation and reports of planned US-Israel strikes on Iran — has pushed Brent to a five-month high, lifting energy and defense while squeezing airlines; meanwhile the AI trade is wobbling as Meta's cash burn and the neocloud rout weigh on tech.
self_check: My record shows high-confidence calls have been my weakest (4 of 12), especially chasing oil spikes the day they happen, while merger and geopolitics ideas have worked best. So today I put my top conviction in a defense name with a structural story rather than a crude-price chase, and sized oil exposure more modestly.

picks.reason: Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, US diplomats evacuating, and a 10-year 850-jet F-35 deal point to sustained defense spending; L3Harris is a leader in electronic warfare and counter-drone systems, an area forecast to grow fast and one the market has connected less directly to this news than Lockheed.

Brent hit a five-month high as the Middle East conflict escalates and Aramco evacuated its Dhahran headquarters; energy has only risen 0.4% in the past week, so the biggest US oil major still has room to catch up if crude stays elevated.

Three major US airlines have now cut 2026 profit forecasts on higher fuel, and American guided to a full-year loss; with crude still climbing, the earnings pain likely keeps unfolding across the group.
Reports that the DOJ could soon approve the Roku/Fox deal narrowed the spread; if clearance lands, the remaining discount should close further.

A Bernstein downgrade and the broader neocloud rout keep pressure on CoreWeave, and Meta's first-ever cash burn on AI raises questions about how long hyperscaler contracts underwrite these balance sheets.
US diplomats ordered out of Saudi Arabia, Iranian naval losses and fresh sanctions all raise the odds of a wider regional war, which typically supports gold.

No major company news; trading with the broader AI-spending sentiment.

No major news; low jobless claims and a firm economy are a mild positive for credit quality.

Regional war risk, US diplomats leaving Saudi Arabia and Iran sanctions keep safe-haven demand for gold firm.

top_buys.pitch: Defense electronics play on a widening Middle East conflict that the market has connected less directly than Lockheed.
top_buys.why: Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, US diplomats being ordered out, and Iranian naval losses all point to higher and longer defense spending. The Pentagon's new 10-year, 850-jet F-35 agreement signals long-term budget commitment that lifts the whole prime contractor group. L3Harris is a leader in electronic warfare and counter-drone, segments forecast to grow around 13% a year. It rose less than Lockheed on yesterday's headlines, leaving catch-up room.
top_buys.risks: A quick de-escalation or ceasefire would unwind the defense bid, and budget politics ahead of midterms could cloud outlays.
top_buys.watch: Any US military response to Iranian/Houthi actions and L3Harris's next quarterly report and backlog figures.

top_buys.pitch: Jet fuel is eating airline profits and three carriers have already cut guidance — with crude still rising, more cuts are likely.
top_buys.why: Southwest became the third major US airline this month to lower its 2026 profit forecast on fuel, and American guided to a full-year loss despite record revenue. Brent just hit a five-month high and the Middle East situation is escalating, not calming. An ETF spreads the bet across carriers so one company's hedging luck doesn't ruin the thesis.
top_buys.risks: A sudden de-escalation would crush oil and send airlines sharply higher; strong holiday booking data could also offset fuel costs.
top_buys.watch: Brent crude direction and the remaining airline earnings reports and guidance updates.

top_buys.pitch: Biggest US oil major with Brent at a five-month high and energy still a laggard this week.
top_buys.why: Brent is at a five-month high as Houthi strikes and an Aramco HQ evacuation threaten Gulf supply, and Reuters commentary warns the recent flow rebound shouldn't be mistaken for normality. Energy stocks rose only 0.4% last week, so the sector hasn't fully repriced sustained higher crude. Exxon's upstream earnings leverage to crude is direct and its scale makes it a default destination for sector inflows.
top_buys.risks: Oil spikes on war headlines often fade quickly if supply is never actually disrupted, and Exxon has already drifted up with the sector.
top_buys.watch: Whether Gulf production is actually disrupted and Exxon's upcoming quarterly results.

top_buys.pitch: Merger arb: DOJ approval of the Fox deal reportedly close, and the spread hasn't fully closed.
top_buys.why: Reports say the Justice Department could soon approve the Roku/Fox transaction, and the deal spread has already begun narrowing. Antitrust clearance is usually the last big binary risk in a deal like this, so confirmation should close the remaining discount. Merger-driven ideas have been my most reliable category.
top_buys.risks: The DOJ could impose conditions or delay, and if the deal breaks Roku likely falls back to standalone valuation.
top_buys.watch: An official DOJ announcement or second-request resolution in the coming days.

top_buys.pitch: The neocloud rout keeps grinding on after a Bernstein downgrade and growing questions about AI capex funding.
top_buys.why: Bernstein cut the stock and price target, and commentary describes mounting hurdles for CoreWeave specifically. Meta just reported its first cash burn since IPO on AI spending, which raises the question of how aggressively hyperscalers keep underwriting leveraged AI infrastructure players. The broader AI trade is under pressure and the neocloud group is the most leveraged part of it.
top_buys.risks: The stock has already fallen hard, so any positive contract news or an AI sentiment bounce could cause a sharp short squeeze.
top_buys.watch: New capacity contract announcements and CoreWeave's next earnings and debt disclosures.

summary.big_story: Middle East escalation — Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, an Aramco HQ evacuation and reported US-Israel plans against Iran — drove Brent to a five-month high and knocked the Dow lower.
summary.top_pick: L3Harris, a defense electronics and counter-drone leader that should benefit from sustained defense budgets but hasn't been bid up as hard as Lockheed on today's news.
summary.watch: Whether crude holds its five-month high and whether DOJ formally clears the Roku/Fox deal.
